Name: Max
Experience: This website is a great tool for parents,guardians and children to learn about the dangers of AI and how we can identify content that's real v.s generated by AI!

Name: Sarah M.
Experience: I recently showed my 12-year-old the "uncanny valley" concept to help her spot deepfakes. We looked for inconsistent lighting on faces and unnatural blinking patterns in viral videos. It’s a great way to build that "verify-first" mindset early on before they encounter more convincing synthetic media.

Name: Principal Jenkins
Experience: We’ve started a "Lateral Reading" challenge in our 8th-grade tech class. Instead of asking if a chatbot’s answer is "true," students must cross-reference claims against three verified, human-authored sources. It’s effectively neutralizing the "appeal to authority" that AI often mimics.

Name: David K.
Experience: My son noticed that his AI image generator only showed one type of person for "successful doctor." We used it as a teaching moment to discuss training data bias and how AI reflects internet prejudices. It really opened his eyes to why we shouldn't take algorithmic output as absolute truth.
